text:
leo: quick signal from the v7-small PTQ bring-up: offline NDCG@10 looks essentially unchanged (+0.0008) but MRR@1 on the short-query cohort dropped ~3.8%. No tokenizer or candidate set diffs between FP32 and PTQ runs.

anya: curious. we've seen similar patterns but would like a slightly different diagnostics surface: can we compute per-query "rank_concordance" (fraction of top-1 preserved FP32->PTQ) and a "confidence_spread" metric (top-1 score minus top-2 score)?

leo: I added probes to the harness. Ran a small seeded sweep: FP32 vs PTQ (static PTQ) on 3 seeds with no-shuffle. Summary:
- NDCG@10: delta +0.0007 (noise)
- MRR@1 (short queries): mean drop 3.8%
- rank_concordance (top1 preserved): FP32->baseline 99.2%, PTQ 95.3% (so ~3.9% of queries had top-1 change)
- median confidence_spread (top1-top2): FP32 0.024, PTQ 0.011 (spread collapsed)

dmitri: that collapse in confidence_spread is convincing evidence that quantization is reducing resolution at the head and allowing reorderings. Two lines to try: (A) preserve last-layer at higher precision (fp16) so logits keep dynamic range, (B) softmax temperature >1.0 or a tiny linear rescale to amplify gaps, (C) deterministic stable tiebreaker (original candidate position) so ties resolve predictably.

carmen: also try a different quant path: dynamic quant vs static PTQ; dynamic quant sometimes preserves more head resolution. Could be a vendor/kernel difference.

samira: I kicked off 6 short experiments (seeded, no-shuffle):
1) static PTQ baseline (control)
2) static PTQ + stable tiebreak (candidate_pos)
3) static PTQ + last-layer fp16
4) static PTQ + softmax temp 1.05
5) dynamic quant (per-channel)
6) static PTQ + tiny deterministic jitter (hash-based) as final tiebreaker
Artifacts logged to CI job 2301.

ci-bot: job-2301 started by samira - artifacts: https://ci.redwood/job/2301/artifacts

samira: compact results (MRR@1 short-query delta vs FP32):
1) baseline: -3.8%
2) tiebreak: -1.1%
3) last-layer fp16: -0.6%
4) temp=1.05: -1.4%
5) dynamic quant: -2.2%
6) jitter-tiebreak: -1.0%
Also rank_concordance (top1 preserved): baseline 95.3%, tiebreak 98.9%, fp16 99.2%. confidence_spread median: baseline 0.011, fp16 0.021.

dmitri: looks like last-layer fp16 is the most effective single fix, lexicographic tiebreaker also helps a lot and is cheap. Dynamic quant is better than baseline but worse than fp16 fallback. Softmax temp helps somewhat but is a slippery knob for calibration. Jitter is a hack; prefer deterministic tiebreak over jitter.

anya: proposed action items:
- add deterministic tiebreaker (score desc, original_pos asc) to the final rank step in eval and prod as a safe fallback (short PR).
- add a rankbench smoke: seeded PTQ run on short-query cohort gating MRR@1 drop <= 1% and rank_concordance >= 99%. Run 3 seeds by default.
- add telemetry metrics: rank_concordance_top1, confidence_spread_p50/p95, topk_exact_tie_frac, and surface them per-model+quant-config.
- add an optional config knob: last_layer_dtype: [quantized|fp16] so we can enable fp16 logits for quant schemes that lose head resolution.

carmen: also add a small unit test for deterministic tie behavior: forces two equal scores and verifies stable ordering by original_pos. And document why this is necessary (quant binning causing ties).

samira: I'll open PR with artifacts (histograms & seed manifests) and include the simple rank_concordance probe code and example dashboards. Will tag eng-ml and qa.

dmitri: one more thought: include a weekly job that runs rankbench PTQ smoketest on a small heldout slice and pushes a regression alert if rank_concordance drops by >0.5% from baseline.

leo: thank you. This gives us a path to keep PTQ while preventing surprising MRR shifts. I'll pick up the prod tie-break PR and the runbook note about enabling last-layer fp16 for quant configs that fail the smoke.

ci-bot: job-2301 completed, artifacts uploaded.

anya: thanks everyone. small fixes + telemetry seems preferable to rollback. Tag me on the PRs and on the infra ticket for the rankbench smoke.
